comparisons.reasoning: Both cover active-project identification, source files, taxonomy, and an ordered C1→C2→C3 plan; neither materially outperforms the other on the stated checklist.
Both require revalidating the active project, rerun list-projects/read-project-summary, reread shared specs, and explicitly call out stale context and wrong C3 parent risks.
A is more complete: it starts from shared specs/project summary, separates kind vs relationship checks, adds exact spelling/level checks, and gives a stronger fallback when the summary looks stale.
Both name c4-modeling-process, but B more clearly defines understand-project-structure as workspace framing and places handoff only after validating project, taxonomy, and relevant files.
B better answers the onboarding angle by stating local conventions first, citing shared/project folders plus .github/skills, giving concrete taxonomy examples, and making the handoff path explicit.
